purpose: One shared authoring contract. Topic manifests supply the scope data; this file supplies the reusable teaching instructions.

pedagogy.audience: Self-study learner; clear English for a non-native speaker; define technical terms on first use.
sequence: Start with the problem this topic solves and a plain-language mental model.
Show how the major parts fit together; give a map before detail.
Explain prerequisites and core concepts in a sensible order.
Walk through behavior step by step using a small end-to-end example.
Only after the conceptual map, explain the supplied named APIs/features in organized groups.
Finish with tradeoffs, common mistakes, debugging, practice, and retrieval questions as appropriate to the lesson type.
quality: Explain why a concept exists, when it is useful, when it is not, and how it relates to neighboring concepts.
Use examples that build in difficulty and explain expected results.
Include edge cases, misconceptions, failure modes, and decision criteria where relevant.
Do not confuse an introductory overview with an exhaustive reference lesson.
Keep the broad overview readable without requiring the learner to memorize every API first.

closedWorld.rule: Do not browse or invent version-specific names. Exact APIs, methods, attributes, language features, alternatives, and release changes may be named only when present in the supplied manifest data or its cited source snapshot.
closedWorld.inventory: A reference lesson explains the supplied inventory names and may not add names. If the inventory is empty or incomplete, report blocked rather than filling it from model memory.
closedWorld.concepts: Teach the supplied concept map. If it is absent, the topic is not ready for generation; do not infer that a title is a complete syllabus.
closedWorld.comparisons: Include comparisons only when manifest.comparisons contains explicit alternatives and evidence. Empty means omit the comparison section.
closedWorld.versions: Include release history only when manifest.versionNotes contains named changes, exact affected versions, and source URLs. Empty means omit version-history discussion; never create a versions lesson for a timeless topic.
closedWorld.code: Never claim an example was executed unless a test result is supplied. Mark unexecuted code examples as unverified and pseudocode as pseudocode.

overview.goal: Give the learner an understandable whole-topic picture before any API catalog.
requiredSections: When to use it and tradeoffs
overview.instruction: Do not turn this into a list of every API. Teach the big picture using manifest.concepts and a simple running example.

concepts.goal: Build conceptual depth in prerequisite order.

reference.goal: Teach one bounded group of exact, pre-enumerated names.
requiredSections: How this group fits the mental model
reference.instruction: Explain every supplied name; do not add names. Keep the reference lesson connected to the overview concepts.

practice.goal: Develop independent problem-solving and practical fluency.
practice.instruction: Use only APIs and features present in the supplied inventory. For DSA, include problem statement, constraints, examples, C# solution, proof idea, dry run, complexity, tests, and alternative approaches where supplied.

interview.goal: Prepare the learner to explain, compare, and reason under interview conditions.

dsaPractice.instruction: Teach a transferable problem-solving pattern. Do not reveal the full solution before the learner has a chance to try. Every stated constraint, example and solution must agree. Explain why the chosen pattern fits and what signals would make it fail.

optionalSections.recentVersionChanges: Add only when manifest.versionNotes is nonempty. Keep the summary brief and focus on the current stable release and a small number of recent relevant major changes.
optionalSections.alternatives: Add only when manifest.comparisons is nonempty.
optionalSections.sources: Cite the supplied source snapshot near the claims it supports. Do not claim independent verification.
